A collection of process dependency type definitions used across all manufacturing process steps in CPRO camera assembly. Contains three enumerated values — SEQUENCE, JOIN, and FORK — each defining a distinct structural relationship between a process step and its predecessors. Referenced by DepType Property in each process step Collection via valueId.
Process dependency type indicating that a single predecessor process must complete before this process begins. Represents a linear one-to-one flow between consecutive manufacturing steps.

Process dependency type indicating that two or more predecessor processes must all complete before this process begins. Represents a convergence point where multiple parallel sub-assembly streams merge into a single downstream process.

Process dependency type indicating that a single predecessor process triggers two or more independent successor processes simultaneously. Represents a divergence point where a completed sub-assembly feeds into multiple parallel downstream process streams.

A manufacturing process step in which firmware is loaded into a camera module PCB via a USB jig board interface. The jig pin must be connected with the power in the OFF state before initiating data transfer. This step is the first in the firmware input sequence and is triggered upon completion of the SMT

A manufacturing process step in which loaded firmware data is verified for compliance with product specification and buyer requirements. No physical input materials are consumed. Verification is performed using the OEM specification document as the reference standard. Input sequence order must be strictly observed to ensure data integrity.

A manufacturing process step that confirms complete and successful loading of firmware data onto the camera module PCB. Completion of firmware input is verified to be 100% before the assembly advances to the next stage. Firmware compliance with product and buyer specification is re-confirmed against the OEM specification document. Input sequence order must be strictly observed.

A manufacturing process step in which a unique MAC address and model name are programmed into a camera module using an input program interface. MAC address uniqueness must be guaranteed across all units to prevent duplication. Model name is verified via device command output. This step concludes the firmware input process group and the sub-assembly proceeds to the focus adjustment process upon completion.

A classification that defines the structural relationship between a manufacturing process and its predecessor processes. SEQUENCE indicates a single predecessor must complete before this process begins. JOIN indicates multiple predecessors must all complete before this process begins. FORK indicates this process branches into multiple independent successor processes.

A controlled vocabulary defining the structural dependency relationship between a manufacturing process step and its predecessor steps. Used in discrete event simulation to determine process execution order and synchronisation conditions.

A process dependency type in which a single predecessor process must be completed before the current process can begin. Represents a linear one-to-one directional flow between consecutive manufacturing steps in a production sequence.

A process dependency type in which two or more predecessor processes must all complete before the current process can begin. Represents a convergence point in the manufacturing flow where multiple parallel sub-assembly streams synchronise and merge into a single downstream process step.

A process dependency type in which the completion of a single predecessor process simultaneously triggers two or more independent successor processes. Represents a divergence point in the manufacturing flow where a completed sub-assembly or intermediate product feeds into multiple parallel downstream process streams.

The identifier of the predecessor process or processes that must be completed before the current manufacturing process step can begin execution. When DepType is SEQUENCE, a single process identifier is specified. When DepType is JOIN, multiple process identifiers are specified as a semicolon-separated list, indicating that all listed predecessors must complete before execution begins.

The time required to complete one unit of work at a manufacturing process step, measured in seconds. Used in discrete event simulation to define the duration of a process step timeout. Represents the standard cycle time under normal operating conditions with the assigned worker group and equipment.

The proportion of non-conforming units produced at a manufacturing process step relative to the total number of units processed. Expressed as a dimensionless decimal value. Used in discrete event simulation to determine stochastic defect occurrence per unit processed at each step.

A list of references to material or sub-assembly entities consumed as input at a specific manufacturing process step. Each entry references an asset defined in the HierarchicalStructures Submodel and carries a quantity qualifier indicating the number of units consumed per production cycle.

A reference element pointing to a specific material or sub-assembly entity in the HierarchicalStructures Submodel that is consumed as input at a manufacturing process step. The quantity consumed per production cycle is expressed via a ValueQualifier.

A manufacturing process group in which a lens holder and actuator sub-assembly are mounted onto a sensor board, and the completed sensor board is subsequently integrated with the main board PCB. This group is an independent process triggered upon SMT completion and proceeds sequentially through two steps before the output sub-assembly is passed to the SET assembly line.

A manufacturing process step in which a lens holder, actuator, lens, and fastening hardware are assembled onto a sensor board sub-assembly. The lens holder geometry is defined by CNC post-processing specification. Torque requirements for fastening must be measured and confirmed periodically using a torque meter. Absence of foreign matter on the TDN filter must be confirmed visually before the step is considered complete.

A fixed-focus M12-mount infrared-compatible lens with 5 megapixel resolution, used in the sensor board sub-assembly of IP camera modules. Characterised by a 1/2.5-inch image sensor format, 4 mm focal length, and F2.0 aperture. Consumed at the SENSOR BOARD assembly process step.

An injection-moulded plastic nut used to secure and fix the lens assembly within the lens holder of an IP camera module. Manufactured from polycarbonate resin and used to maintain lens position stability after torque fastening during sensor board assembly.

displayName.text: DC Lens Holder M12 with TDN Mount

definition.text: A zinc die-cast lens holder with M12 thread and integrated TDN actuator mount, used to position and retain the lens assembly in an IP camera module. CNC post-processing ensures dimensional accuracy of the lens seating surface and TDN mounting interface. Consumed at the SENSOR BOARD assembly process step.

A True Day and Night optical actuator module used in IP camera assemblies to switch between day and night imaging modes by mechanically repositioning an infrared cut filter. Characterised by low magnetic interference design to minimise electromagnetic noise in proximity to image sensor circuits. Consumed at the SENSOR BOARD assembly process step.

A small Phillips-head machine screw used to fasten mechanical sub-assembly components in IP camera module manufacturing. Black surface finish applied for corrosion resistance and aesthetic consistency. Torque application must be controlled within specification to prevent thread stripping or component damage during assembly.

A thin flame-retardant sponge pad placed between the lens holder assembly and the PCB surface to provide electrical insulation and mechanical cushioning. Prevents direct contact between metallic lens holder components and PCB circuitry, reducing risk of short circuit and absorbing assembly-induced mechanical stress.

A cross-head machine screw used to fasten the lens holder sub-assembly to the main board PCB in IP camera module manufacturing. Black surface finish applied for corrosion resistance. Designated as a lens holder standard fastener for common use across applicable camera module variants. Torque must be applied within specification to prevent PCB damage or lens holder misalignment.

displayName.text: DC Gimbal Front Housing HIGH POWER 2IR

definition.text: A die-cast aluminium front housing component for a gimbal sub-assembly in an IP dome camera module. Provides the structural enclosure for the infrared PCB and IR rubber seal. Surface is black anodised for corrosion resistance and thermal management. Component version must be managed sequentially per stock depletion instructions.

displayName.text: SENSOR BOARD Integration onto Main Board (Process 20-1)

definition.text: A manufacturing process step in which a completed sensor board sub-assembly is integrated with the main board PCB using insulation seat and fastening screws. Correct TDN actuator orientation must be confirmed against reference photograph. Absence of foreign matter and connector integrity are verified visually before the step is considered complete. Completed sub-assemblies are transferred to the subsequent assembly line in batches via cart.

A manufacturing process group in which the optical focus of a camera module is adjusted and verified after sensor board integration. Focus quality is assessed visually using a dome cover as reference. Lens protrusion is measured to ensure correct focal length. Connector integrity and absence of foreign matter are confirmed before the process group is considered complete. This group receives output from the firmware input process group and feeds into the SET assembly line.

A manufacturing process step in which the optical focus of a camera module is adjusted and verified following sensor board sub-assembly integration. A dome cover is used as a reference fixture during visual focus inspection. Lens protrusion length is measured using a vernier caliper to confirm correct focal distance. No physical input materials are consumed at this step.

A manufacturing process group in which a gimbal housing, infrared PCB, and associated hardware are assembled into a gimbal sub-assembly, which is subsequently integrated with the sensor board sub-assembly at a JOIN convergence point. The group begins as an independent process upon SMT completion and merges with the sensor board assembly stream before proceeding to the combined assembly stage.

A manufacturing process step in which a gimbal front housing, infrared PCB, infrared rubber seal, and fastening screws are assembled into a gimbal sub-assembly unit. Correct orientation and seating of the infrared rubber component must be confirmed visually against a reference photograph. This step begins independently upon SMT completion and its output converges with the sensor board sub-assembly at the subsequent JOIN process step.

displayName.text: IR Rubber Seal Mini Dome Camera

definition.text: A rubber sealing component used in dome camera gimbal assemblies to provide environmental sealing and mechanical cushioning between the infrared PCB and the gimbal front housing. Correct directional orientation must be confirmed during assembly to ensure proper seating and sealing performance. Component integrity must be verified visually to confirm absence of tears or damage before assembly proceeds.

A cross-head machine screw used to fasten infrared PCB and housing components in IP dome camera gimbal sub-assembly manufacturing. Black surface finish applied for corrosion resistance. Torque must be applied within specification to prevent thread stripping or component damage. Designated for CCTV camera assembly applications.

An injection-moulded polycarbonate bracket used to mount and retain the gimbal module assembly within an IP dome camera housing. Provides structural support for the TDN actuator interface and IR harness routing. Harness orientation must be confirmed against reference during assembly to prevent wire pinching or disconnection.

An injection-moulded polycarbonate tilt bracket used to enable angular adjustment of the gimbal sub-assembly within an IP dome camera housing. Provides the mechanical interface for tilt axis movement. Correct centre alignment between the IR rubber seal and lens must be verified visually during assembly to ensure optical axis integrity.

displayName.text: Tapping Screw D2.0x15.0 SUS Black Half-Thread

definition.text: A stainless steel cross-head tapping screw with half-thread configuration used to fasten bracket components in IP dome camera gimbal sub-assembly manufacturing. Half-thread design provides controlled clamping force distribution across the fastening interface. Black surface finish applied for corrosion resistance. Torque must be applied within specification to prevent thread damage or bracket deformation.

A manufacturing process step at which the gimbal sub-assembly and the sensor board sub-assembly converge and are integrated into a single unit. Gimbal module bracket and tilt bracket are fastened using tapping screws. IR harness routing direction and optical centre alignment between lens and IR rubber seal must be confirmed visually before the step is considered complete. This step is a JOIN convergence point in the assembly flow.

A die-cast aluminium bottom case housing component for mini dome IP camera assemblies. Provides the lower structural enclosure into which cable routing components, waterproof cable, and cable tie are assembled. Component version must be managed sequentially per stock depletion instructions.

A rubber grommet component used to seal the cable entry point of a waterproof IP camera bottom case housing. Provides environmental sealing around the external cable, preventing ingress of moisture and contaminants. Dimensional compatibility with cable outer diameter must be confirmed before installation.

displayName.text: Waterproof Cable Assembly RJ45 and DC Jack

definition.text: A pre-assembled waterproof cable harness integrating an RJ45 network connector and a DC power jack, used for external connectivity of IP dome camera modules. Provides sealed cable entry into the bottom case housing through a rubber grommet. Cable outer diameter and connector type must be confirmed compatible with the specific PCB variant before assembly.

A disposable nylon cable tie used to bundle and secure internal cable assemblies within a camera housing during manufacturing. White colour finish for visual identification in assembly. Single-use consumable item replaced at each production cycle.

A thermally conductive rubber pad used in IP camera module assemblies to facilitate heat transfer between the PCB and the metal housing. Provides both thermal management and mechanical cushioning between the board and case surfaces. Correct positioning must be confirmed to ensure full contact coverage for effective thermal performance.

A manufacturing process group in which the bottom case housing is assembled with cable routing components and waterproof cable, subsequently integrated with the focus-adjusted sub-assembly at a JOIN convergence point, and completed with gimbal support and rotation limit bracket installation. The group spans both SEMI and SET worker group assignments across its three constituent steps.

A manufacturing process step in which the bottom case housing is assembled with a cable rubber grommet, waterproof cable harness, and cable tie. Cable routing and tie securing must be confirmed before the step is considered complete. This step begins independently upon SMT completion and its output converges with the focus adjustment sub-assembly at the subsequent JOIN process step.

A cross-head machine screw designated for common use across multiple assembly steps in IP dome camera manufacturing. Used to fasten PCB and bracket components onto the bottom case housing. Black surface finish applied for corrosion resistance. Torque must be applied within specification to prevent thread stripping or component damage. Quantity consumed varies per process step and must be confirmed against the applicable process instruction.

A micro coaxial wire harness used to transmit high-frequency image signals between the image sensor PCB and the main processing board in an IP camera module. Characterised by a 40-pin parallel micro coaxial configuration with AWG42 conductor gauge for minimal signal attenuation. Pre-assembled with core connector upon incoming inspection to ensure connection integrity before integration into the camera module assembly.

A die-cast aluminium structural bracket used to support and retain the gimbal sub-assembly within the bottom case housing of an IP dome camera module. Black anodised surface finish applied for corrosion resistance. Fastened to the bottom case using cross-head machine screws with controlled torque application.

displayName.text: Sponge Gimbal Support Bracket Pad VD7

definition.text: A sponge cushioning pad applied to the gimbal support bracket surface in IP dome camera assemblies to prevent direct mechanical contact between the bracket and adjacent components. Provides vibration damping and surface protection during and after assembly. Correct placement must be confirmed against the reference photograph to ensure full bracket surface coverage.

An injection-moulded polycarbonate bracket used to mechanically limit the rotational travel range of a gimbal sub-assembly within an IP dome camera housing. Prevents gimbal over-rotation that could cause cable pinching or connector damage during camera pan and tilt adjustment. Installation orientation must be confirmed against reference to ensure correct constraint direction.

A manufacturing process step at which the bottom case sub-assembly and the focus-adjusted camera sub-assembly converge and are integrated. The main board PCB is thermally coupled to the housing via a thermal pad and mechanically fastened using screws. Signal connectivity between the sensor board and main board is established via micro coaxial wire harness. This step is a JOIN convergence point in the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which gimbal support and rotation limit bracket components are installed onto the integrated bottom case sub-assembly to complete the bottom case assembly stage. Gimbal support bracket with sponge pad is fastened using machine screws with controlled torque. Rotation limits bracket orientation must be confirmed against reference to ensure correct mechanical constraint direction. Completed sub-assemblies are transferred to the subsequent assembly line in batches via cart.

A manufacturing process group in which the gimbal sub-assembly and the bottom case sub-assembly converge and are mechanically integrated into a single combined unit. MCX cable connectivity and gimbal directional orientation are confirmed visually during assembly. This group constitutes a JOIN convergence point receiving outputs from two independent assembly streams before proceeding to the inspection process group.

description.text: GIMBAL + BOTTOM ASS'Y (Process 60)

definition.text: A manufacturing process step at which the gimbal sub-assembly and the bottom case sub-assembly are mechanically fastened together using cross-head screws. MCX cable connectivity between the sensor board and main board is confirmed for complete insertion and absence of damage. Gimbal directional orientation is verified against reference photograph. This step is a JOIN convergence point receiving outputs from the gimbal assembly and bottom case assembly streams.

A manufacturing process group in which the assembled camera module undergoes functional and visual inspection across three sequential steps. Inspection operations are performed by a dedicated inspection sub-group allocated from within the SET assembly worker group. No physical input materials are consumed during inspection. Units identified as non-conforming are diverted to the RMA repair process.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the first stage of functional and visual inspection. Inspection is performed by a dedicated sub-group within the SET assembly worker group. Units identified as non-conforming at this step are diverted to the RMA repair process before re-entering the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the second stage of functional and visual inspection following the first inspection stage. Inspection is performed by a dedicated sub-group within the SET assembly worker group. Units identified as non-conforming at this step are diverted to the RMA repair process before re-entering the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the third and final stage of functional and visual inspection. Upon successful completion, the inspected sub-assembly proceeds to the SET assembly JOIN process where it merges with the upper housing sub-assembly. Units identified as non-conforming are diverted to the RMA repair process.

A manufacturing process group in which the upper housing components of an IP dome camera module are assembled, including the outer dome cover, gasket sealing, vent adhesive, and mechanical fastening. This group is an independent process triggered upon SMT completion and proceeds sequentially through two steps before the completed upper housing sub-assembly merges with the inspected camera assembly at the SET assembly JOIN process.

A self-adhesive pressure equalisation vent used in sealed electronic enclosures to balance internal and external air pressure while preventing ingress of moisture, dust, and contaminants. Integrity of the adhesive bond and absence of physical damage must be confirmed visually after attachment to ensure effective sealing performance.

displayName.text: DC Upper Case Mini Dome UDP

definition.text: A die-cast aluminium upper housing component for mini dome IP camera modules. Forms the outer structural enclosure that houses the dome cover, bubble gasket, vent, and dome stopper sub-assembly. Surface finish and press geometry must conform to the current engineering change order specification. Foreign matter must be absent from all internal surfaces before assembly proceeds.

displayName.text: Injection-Moulded Dome Cover Micro CR Dome Black Print

definition.text: An outsourced injection-moulded optical dome cover used as the outer transparent enclosure of an IP dome camera upper housing. Black surface printing is applied to the designated areas per product specification. Inner dome surface must be free of foreign matter, scratches, and contamination to prevent optical interference during camera operation.

A rubber bubble gasket used to provide environmental sealing between the dome cover and the upper case of an IP dome camera module. Prevents ingress of moisture, dust, and contaminants through the dome cover interface. Correct directional orientation must be confirmed against reference photograph during assembly to ensure uniform sealing pressure distribution around the dome perimeter.

displayName.text: Press Dome Stopper EN672 Mini Dome

definition.text: A press-formed metal dome stopper component used to mechanically secure the dome cover within the upper case of an IP mini dome camera module. Prevents axial and rotational displacement of the dome cover during handling and operation. Component version must be verified against the current engineering change order specification before installation.

displayName.text: Machine Screw M3x4.0 White Phillips Head

definition.text: A white Phillips cross-head machine screw used to fasten upper case housing components in IP dome camera assembly. White surface finish applied for visual identification and corrosion resistance. Torque must be applied within specification to prevent thread stripping or housing surface damage during fastening.

A rubber sealing gasket used as the primary environmental seal between the upper and lower housing assemblies of an IP mini dome camera module. Provides protection against ingress of moisture, dust, and contaminants through the housing interface. Correct seating within the case groove must be confirmed before fastening to ensure uniform compression and sealing integrity around the full perimeter.

A Torx drive machine screw used to fasten the upper and lower housing assemblies of an IP dome camera module into a sealed enclosure. Torx 20 drive interface provides improved torque transfer and reduced cam-out risk compared to Phillips head fasteners. Torque must be applied within specification to prevent thread damage or housing surface scratching during final assembly closure.

A manufacturing process step in which the upper housing sub-assembly is constructed by integrating the dome cover, bubble gasket, dome stopper, and adhesive vent onto the upper case. All sealing and retention components must be confirmed correctly oriented and free of foreign matter before mechanical fastening. This step begins independently upon SMT completion and its output merges with the inspected camera assembly at the SET assembly JOIN process.

A manufacturing process step in which the main gasket is installed into the upper case housing groove and the upper and lower camera housings are mechanically joined using Torx screws. Correct gasket seating and absence of foreign matter must be confirmed before fastening. This step completes the upper housing sub-assembly which subsequently merges with the inspected camera assembly at the SET assembly JOIN process.

A manufacturing process group in which the inspected camera sub-assembly and the completed upper housing sub-assembly are joined into a finished camera unit. IR sponge cleaning and dome cover protection film attachment are performed at this convergence point. This group constitutes the final assembly JOIN step before the product proceeds to the aging test process.

A light-absorbing sponge component used in IP dome camera assemblies to suppress infrared light leakage and internal reflection between the IR PCB and the upper housing enclosure. The component must be cleaned with methyl alcohol prior to installation to remove surface oils and contaminants that could degrade optical performance. Cleaning effectiveness must be confirmed visually before assembly proceeds.

protective adhesive film applied to the outer dome cover surface of an IP dome camera to prevent scratches and surface contamination during final assembly operations and subsequent handling. Applied at the SET assembly stage following housing closure. Full adhesion without lifting or positional misalignment must be confirmed before the assembled unit proceeds to the next process stage.

A manufacturing process step at which the inspected camera sub-assembly and the completed upper housing sub-assembly are mechanically joined into a finished camera unit. IR sponge is cleaned and installed to suppress infrared leakage. Dome cover protective film is applied to prevent surface damage during subsequent handling. This step is a JOIN convergence point constituting the final mechanical assembly stage before aging test.

A manufacturing process group in which fully assembled electronic products are operated under normal or accelerated conditions for a defined duration to identify and eliminate early-stage failure mechanisms prior to shipment. Units that exhibit anomalous behaviour during aging are diverted for inspection or repair. This group follows the final mechanical assembly stage and precedes the packaging process.

A manufacturing process step in which a fully assembled camera unit is operated continuously for a defined duration to detect latent defects and early-stage failure mechanisms. Units that fail or exhibit anomalous behaviour during the aging period are removed from the production flow and directed to corrective action before shipment.

A manufacturing process group in which the finished camera unit is packaged with all required accessories, protective materials, and documentation into an individual unit box and subsequently into a shipping carton. Product label attachment is performed by a dedicated labelling worker group. Accessory completeness and label specification compliance must be confirmed before the packaging process is considered complete.

An injection-moulded plastic mounting nut supplied as a field installation accessory with IP dome camera products. Used during on-site camera mounting to secure the camera housing to the installation surface. Accessory completeness must be confirmed before unit packaging is sealed.

A machined metal mounting bolt supplied as a field installation accessory with IP dome camera products. Used in conjunction with the mounting nut to secure the camera housing to the installation surface during on-site deployment. Accessory completeness must be confirmed before unit packaging is sealed.

A Torx T20 drive L-shaped wrench tool supplied as a field installation accessory with IP dome camera products. Enables end users to fasten and adjust Torx head screws during on-site camera installation without requiring separate tooling. Accessory completeness must be confirmed before unit packaging is sealed.

A Phillips cross-head tapping screw supplied as a field installation accessory with IP dome camera products. Used by end users to fix the camera mounting bracket to walls or ceilings during on-site installation. Material specification changed from nickel to stainless steel finish to improve corrosion resistance. Accessory completeness must be confirmed before unit packaging is sealed.

A resealable antistatic zipper bag used to enclose electronic products and accessories during packaging, storage, and transport. Provides electrostatic discharge protection to sensitive electronic components. Zipper closure enables repeated opening and resealing without compromising antistatic properties.

A resealable antistatic zipper bag of larger dimension used to enclose the camera unit and associated accessories during packaging, storage, and transport. Provides electrostatic discharge protection to sensitive electronic components. Used in conjunction with the smaller antistatic bag variant to separately enclose the camera body and accessory items within the same product package.

A rubber waterproof cap fitted over the RJ45 connector of an IP camera cable assembly to prevent moisture, dust, and contaminant ingress at the connector interface during field installation and outdoor operation. Supplied as a packaging accessory for end user application. Ensures continued waterproof rating compliance of the cable assembly after field connection.

displayName.text: Unit Box CVD8 Mini Dome Common

definition.text: An individual product packaging box used to enclose a single camera unit together with its protective foam inserts and moisture absorbent during the unit boxing stage of the packaging process. Common design shared across CVD8 and mini dome camera variants. Box structural integrity and absence of moulding defects must be confirmed before the camera unit is placed inside.

displayName.text: PE Foam Bottom Insert Mini Dome

definition.text: A polyethylene foam bottom insert moulded to the profile of the mini dome camera housing, placed at the base of the individual product box to provide shock absorption and positional retention during storage and transport. Moulding quality must be confirmed free of deformation or surface defects before use to ensure correct camera seating and adequate protection.

A silica gel desiccant packet placed inside the individual product packaging box to absorb ambient moisture and maintain a low-humidity environment during product storage and transport. Prevents condensation on electronic components and corrosion of metal contacts caused by humidity exposure. Desiccant must be confirmed present before box closure to ensure product integrity throughout the distribution chain.

displayName.text: PE Foam Top Insert Mini Dome

definition.text: A polyethylene foam top insert moulded to the profile of the mini dome camera housing, placed over the camera unit inside the individual product box to provide upper shock absorption and secure positional retention during storage and transport. Moulding quality must be confirmed free of deformation or surface defects before use to ensure correct camera retention and adequate protection.

A printed paper or card template supplied as an installation accessory with IP dome camera products, used by end users to mark precise mounting hole positions on the installation surface prior to drilling. Ensures correct spatial alignment of mounting holes for the camera base during on-site installation.

displayName.text: CD Manual IP Camera White Common

definition.text: A CD-ROM product manual supplied as a documentation accessory with IP camera products, providing installation guides, configuration instructions, and operational specifications for end users. Common design shared across applicable IP camera variants with no product-specific printing. Presence must be confirmed before packaging closure to ensure complete accessory delivery to the end user.

An outer corrugated carton shipping box used to consolidate multiple individually packaged IP dome camera units for bulk storage and transport. Designed for the mini dome camera SEON variant. Label specification and attachment position must be confirmed before carton closure to ensure correct product identification throughout the distribution chain. One carton box accommodates eight individual camera units.

A manufacturing process step in which all field installation accessories are prepared and packaged alongside the finished camera unit. Accessory items include mounting hardware, a drive tool, antistatic protective bags, and a waterproof connector cap. Completeness of all accessory items must be confirmed by visual inspection before the unit proceeds to the individual box packaging step.

A manufacturing process step in which the finished camera unit is placed into an individual product box together with a PE foam bottom insert for cushioning and a silica gel desiccant for moisture control. Box structural integrity and foam insert moulding quality must be confirmed before the camera unit is placed inside. Accessory completeness is verified before box closure.

A manufacturing process step in which the PE foam top insert is placed over the camera unit inside the individual product box and the product identification label is attached to the box exterior. Label print specification compliance and serial number uniqueness must be confirmed before the box proceeds to carton packaging. Foam insert moulding quality is verified visually at this step.

A manufacturing process step in which the individually boxed camera unit is consolidated into a shipping carton together with a mount template and CD manual. Eight individual unit boxes are packed per carton. Packaging material completeness and label specification compliance must be confirmed before carton closure. This step constitutes the final stage of the camera module manufacturing and packaging sequence.

The estimated rated power consumption in kilowatts allocated to a manufacturing process node, derived from the total rated power of shared equipment distributed proportionally by process cycle time ratio within the same provess group.

A collection of inventory policy definitions grouped by part category for CPRO. Each child collection represents one part category and carries the minimum stock threshold, maximum stock target, and order ratio used by the warehouse replenishment simulation

A passive two-terminal electrical component that limits or relulates the flow of electrical current in a circuit. Used as an SMT-mounted component in CPRO PCB assemblies, supplied in tape-and-reel format.
The minimum inventory quantity for a part category below which a replenishment order is placed.
The maximum inventory quantity for a part category up to which stock is replenished upon a replenishment order. Defines the upper bound of the inventory replenishment range.
A scalar ratio applied to the expected demand quantity to determine the replenishment order quantity for a part category. A value of 1.0 orders exactly the expected demand quantity.
A passive two-terminal electrical component that stores and releases electrical energy in an electric field. Used as an SMT-mounted component in CPRO PCB assemblies, supplied in tape-and-reel format.

A transparent optical component that focuses light onto the image sensor. In CCTV camera manufacturing, it is a precision-molded or glass lens assembly critical for image quality, supplied as a completed module for integration into the camera.
Injection-molded plastic components used for camera housings, brackets, domes, and structural parts. Manufactured through high-precision plastic injection molding process.
Transparent protective dome cover made of polycarbonate or acrylic, used to protect the camera lens and internal components while maintaining optical clarity in dome-type IP cameras.
Pre-assembled functional unit consisting of multiple components, such as sensor board modules, lens modules, or IR LED modules, ready for integration into the main camera assembly.
Mechanical fastening component used to assemble camera housing, brackets, and internal structures. Includes machine screws, tapping screws, and special screws with various head types and materials.
Rubber sealing components including O-rings and gaskets used to ensure waterproof and dustproof performance (IP66/IP67) of camera housings by preventing ingress of moisture and dust.
Cables, flexible printed circuit boards (FPCB), and wiring harnesses used for electrical connections between main board, sensor board, IR board, and external interfaces in camera assemblies.
Electromechanical component used to establish electrical connections between different parts of the camera, such as between PCBs, cables, sensors, and external interfaces.
A semiconductor device that allows current to flow in one direction only. Used for rectification, protection, switching, and signal modulation in camera PCB circuits.
Surface-mount inductive components used for noise filtering, power supply decoupling, and EMI suppression in camera electronic circuits.
A semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electronic signals and electrical power. Widely used in camera circuits for power management, signal processing, and control functions.
Secondary printed circuit boards (sub-PCBs) including sensor boards, IR control boards, and interface boards that are assembled separately and then integrated into the main PCB.
Image sensor component (CCD or CMOS) that converts optical images into electronic signals. It is one of the most critical components determining the camera's image quality and performance.
Pre-assembled bundle of wires, cables, and connectors used to transmit electrical signals and power between various components and PCBs inside the camera.
Electrical components including switches for power or mode control and fuses for circuit protection against overcurrent.
Devices that detect physical phenomena such as light (image sensor), motion, temperature, or humidity and convert them into electrical signals for processing in the camera system.
Printed Circuit Board populated with Surface Mount Technology (SMT) components, serving as the main electronic backbone of the camera.
Electronic component that generates precise clock signals using the mechanical resonance of a vibrating crystal. Essential for timing and synchronization in digital camera circuits.
Materials and supplies that are consumed during the manufacturing process, such as adhesives, solder paste, cleaning agents, and other auxiliary materials.
